Va_3CEb_.md.evidence: Independent verse discourse on its own subject (ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས), with homage and Sanskrit/Tibetan title formula; no gloss markers, 82% metrical; colophon ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་གཏམ་སློབ་དཔོན་དབྱིག་གཉེན་གྱིས་མཛད་པ names no other work.

Va_3CEc_.md.evidence: Verse treatise stating its own intent (ཚོགས་ནི་གང་གིས་རྫོགས་འགྱུར་དང་ ... དེ་ནི་ལེགས་པར་བཤད་པར་བྱ); 94% metrical, no gloss markers, contains no other file; colophon ཚོགས་ཀྱི་གཏམ.

Va_3CEd_.md.evidence: Title word བཤད་པ notwithstanding, the text is independent verses on the faults of the five sense pleasures (deer, elephant, moth, fish, bee); no gloss markers and no quoted root.

Di_3CEe_.md.evidence: Verse praise of the Buddha (94% metrical) in chapters; colophon says སྤེལ་མར་བསྟོད་པ was made jointly by མ་ཏི་ཙི་ཊ and ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གླང་པོ, a composition rather than an explanation; no line-by-line glossing found.

Di_3CEi_.md.evidence: A single four-line realisation song attributed to ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གླང་པོས་སྨྲས་པ, part of the collection named in the colophon (གྲུབ་ཐོབ་ལྔ་བཅུའི་རྟོགས་པ་བརྗོད་པ); it explains no other text.

Di_3CEj_.md.evidence: A short vajra-song of instruction (ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གླང་པོའི་ཞལ་ནས ... གསུང་ངོ) from the collection named in the title; it stands on its own and glosses nothing.

Di_3CEk_.md.evidence: Verse praise of Mañjughoṣa with title formula, homage and dedication; no gloss markers; colophon བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་འཇམ་པའི་དབྱངས་ཀྱི་བསྟོད་པ names no other work.

Di_3CEl_.md.evidence: A verse summary of one sūtra: the closing calls itself བསྡུས་དོན and says ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་མ་ནི། །བརྒྱད་སྟོང་ཡང་དག་བསྡུས་པ; the opening explains the sūtra's framing elements (teacher, witness, place, time). It has no gloss markers, and no file in the corpus is found inside it.

Di_3CEn_.md.evidence: Independent verse meditation instruction (བློ་དང་ལྡན་པས་རྣལ་འབྱོར་བརྩོན་པར་བྱ) with title formula and dedication; 81% metrical, no gloss markers, contains no other file.

Di_3CEq_.md.evidence: Verse treatise whose opening states its own aim (ཚད་མ་སྒྲུབ་ཕྱིར་རང་གི་གཞུང་ཀུན་ལས། །བཏུས་ཏེ ... འདིར་གཅིག་བྱ); 95% metrical, gloss markers 0.14/1000. Its text is found in the commentary Di_3CEr_.md (ཚད་མ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པའི་འགྲེལ་པ). It shares only ~16% with Di_3CEp_.md, another version of the same work.

Di_3CEs_.md.evidence: Short verse treatise on its own subject (the object of cognition); 80% metrical, no gloss markers; 55% of its text is found in Di_3CEt_.md, titled དམིགས་པ་བརྟག་པའི་འགྲེལ་པ, its commentary.

Di_3CEu_.md.evidence: Independent verse treatise (92% metrical) examining the three times, no gloss markers, contains no other file; colophon དུས་གསུམ་བརྟག་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ names no other work.

Di_3CEv_.md.evidence: A prakaraṇa that opens with its own summary verse (ཅེས་པ་བསྟན་བཅོས་བསྡུས་པའོ) and expounds thesis, reason and example in prose. Its ཞེས་པ markers close its own statements rather than quote another text, and it contains no other file. Colophon: རིགས་པར་འཇུག་པའི་སྒོ.

Di_3CEw_.md.evidence: Prose manual (translated from Chinese) opening with its own summary verse and expounding the definitions of proof. No gloss markers, contains no other file; colophon notes it is known as རིགས་པའི་སྒོ.

Di_3CEx_.md.evidence: Verse treatise announcing its own subject (གཏན་ཚིགས་ཚུལ་གསུམ་འཁོར་ལོ་ཡི། །གཏན་ལ་དབབ་པ་བཤད་པར་བྱ); 80% metrical, no gloss markers, contains no other file.

Dh_3CEy_.md.evidence: Verse praise and lament on the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, with title formula, homage and dedication; no gloss markers, contains no other file.

Dh_3CF0.md.evidence: A continuous prose praise (བསྟོད་པ་རྒྱུན་ཆགས) of Vajraḍāka addressing the deity directly; no gloss markers, contains no other file.

Dh_3CF1.md.evidence: Verse ritual manual giving mandala line measurements (ཐིག་གི་ཆོ་ག); no gloss markers, contains no other file.

Dh_3CF2.md.evidence: A long ritual manual (དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག) giving procedure step by step. It says it draws on the root tantra (རྩ་བའི་རྒྱུད་ལས་བཏུས་ནས) but does not quote and gloss it (0.25 gloss markers/1000), and it contains no other file.

Dh_3CF3.md.evidence: A sādhana (སྒྲུབ་ཐབས) giving practice instructions and mantras; no gloss markers, contains no other file. An editorial note at the end discusses its authorship.

Dh_3CF5.md.evidence: The verse work ཚད་མ་རྣམ་འགྲེལ་གྱི་ཚིག་ལེའུར་བྱས་པ (99% metrical, 0.05 gloss markers/1000), whose title word འགྲེལ does not make it a commentary. It contains no other file. 16% of its text is found in Dh_3CFB.md (ཚད་མ་རྣམ་འགྲེལ་གྱི་འགྲེལ་པ), which comments on it.

Dh_3CF6.md.evidence: The opening states its own purpose (མི་མཁས་པ་རྣམས་ལ་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་དུ་འདི་བརྩམ་མོ). Its ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི markers mostly label its own interim verses (ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་བར་སྐབས་ཀྱི་ཚིགས་སུ...) rather than quote another work. The 25% overlap with Dh_3CF7.md looks like shared material from the same author; the text never presents that file as its root.

Dh_3CF7.md.evidence: Prose prakaraṇa that opens by stating its own subject (ཡང་དག་པའི་ཤེས་པ ... དེ་བསྟན་ཏོ) and contains no other file. Its high marker count (8.01/1000) comes from explaining its own example statements (e.g. ... ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་སྦྱོར་བ), not from following another text.

Dh_3CF8.md.evidence: Prose prakaraṇa whose opening states its own purpose (དེ་བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་རྟོགས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར། མདོར་བསྡུས་ནས་འདི་བརྩམ་མོ). It sets out its own verse thesis and argues it, with few gloss markers (0.67/1000) and no other file contained.

Dh_3CF9.md.evidence: Verse treatise examining relation (87% metrical, no gloss markers, contains no other file). 25% of its text is found in Dh_3CFA.md, titled འབྲེལ་པ་བརྟག་པའི་འགྲེལ་པ, its commentary.
